title: Computation of DC Biases in a Resistor Bridge Using PySpice

questions.q: What is meant by DC bias or operating point in PySpice?
questions.a: DC bias (operating point) is the steady-state DC voltage at every node and DC current through every branch when only constant DC sources are applied.

questions.q: Why must every SPICE circuit include `circuit.gnd`?
questions.a: SPICE solves nodal matrix equations relative to a 0 V reference node (`circuit.gnd`). Without ground, the conductance matrix is singular and node voltages are undefined.

questions.q: How do you run a DC bias simulation in PySpice?
questions.a: Create a simulator with `simulator = circuit.simulator(temperature=25, nominal_temperature=25)` and call `analysis = simulator.operating_point()`.

questions.q: What role does R5 play in Experiment 1?
questions.a: R5 is the central bridge resistor connected between Node 3 and Node 2, coupling the left and right voltage divider arms.

questions.q: How are node voltages extracted from the `analysis` object in Experiment 1?
questions.a: By looping over `for node in analysis.nodes.values():` and converting `str(node)` for the node name and `float(node)` for its voltage in volts.

questions.q: What does `2@u_kΩ` or `2@u_kOhm` mean in PySpice?
questions.a: The `@` operator attaches a physical unit from `PySpice.Unit` (`kOhm` = 10^3 ohms) to a numeric value.

questions.q: Which components share Node 2 in the Experiment 1 resistor bridge?
questions.a: R1 (from Node 1 to Node 2), R3 (from Node 2 to GND), and R5 (between Node 3 and Node 2) all meet at Node 2.

questions.q: Why is Node 2 at 4.0 V and Node 3 at 6.0 V in Experiment 1?
questions.a: Solving KCL: at Node 2, (V2-10)/2k + V2/1k + (V2-V3)/2k = 0 => 2V2 - V3 = 2; at Node 3, (V3-10)/1k + V3/2k + (V3-V2)/2k = 0 => -V2 + 4V3 = 20. Solving gives V2 = 4 V and V3 = 6 V.

questions.q: What happens if you accidentally connect both ends of R5 to Node 2?
questions.a: R5 becomes short-circuited across a single node, which invalidates the bridge topology and triggers a short-circuit validation error.

questions.q: When would the voltage across R5 become zero in Experiment 1?
questions.a: When the bridge is balanced, i.e., R1 * R4 = R2 * R3, making V(2) equal to V(3).
